statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58040 is a TLS host verification bypass in the Node.js HTTPS Agent, and an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48934: a request that passes its own checkServerIdentity callback could resume a TLS session or reuse a kept-alive socket that was set up under a different identity policy, so its own hostname verification was skipped. Node.js fixed it for 24.x in 24.18.1, released 2026-07-29: the July 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2026-security-releases, lists 24.x among the affected release lines, and the 24.18.1 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.18.1, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/95ba2cfde7 ('https: bind identity checks to session reuse'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-58040 and is in the v24.18.1 tag and not in v24.18.0; outside its test and the doc/api/https.md documentation it changes lib/https.js. The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-58040, lists Node.js 24 releases up to 24.18.0 as affected. The DHI nodejs-24 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version. Each published nodejs-24 package holds one file, /usr/bin/node, a dynamically linked musl program that carries the Node.js JavaScript library and the C++ runtime where this code lives; the nodejs-24-dev subpackages hold C and C++ header files and two .gypi build configuration files under /usr/include/node, and the nodejs-24-doc subpackages hold the node man page and two debugger helper files, gdbinit and lldb_commands.py, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O file in either. We checked the node binary, /usr/bin/node, in every nodejs-24 package for Alpine 3.23 published by 2026-11-27, on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 24.18.1-r0, 24.19.0-r0, 24.20.0-r0, 24.21.0-r0, 24.22.0-r0, 24.22.1-r0, 24.22.1-r1, 24.22.2-r0 and 24.22.3-r0 report v24.18.1 through v24.22.3 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 24.13.0-r0, 24.13.1-r0, 24.14.0-r0, 24.14.1-r0, 24.15.0-r0, 24.15.0-r1, 24.16.0-r0, 24.17.0-r0 and 24.18.0-r0 report v24.13.0 through v24.18.0 and are affected. As a check, the source of lib/https.js embedded in the node binary contains the per-request identity marker this fix adds (the 'per-request checkServerIdentity' symbol and hasAgentCheckServerIdentity()), which keeps such requests out of session reuse and the socket pool, in 24.18.1-r0 and every later build on both architectures, and does not in any earlier build. 24.18.1-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
